visual_assessment.reviewed_material: phase orbits, grip and empty-hand closeups, isolated crown views, ground/aerial/close-action sequence sheets
resolved_findings: Anatomical left/right had been mirrored despite correct-looking bone names
Empty fingers moved as one rigid plate and had no independent distal pivots
Thrust, downward cuts and grab release leaned away from the intended movement
Waterfowl held the sword at shoulder height instead of overhead
Generic aerial poses did not distinguish Waterfowl, phantom release and Aeonia
A rear crown review angle was occluded by the new high wing posture; isolated head views now cover it
observations: The weapon is on anatomical right; the left hand remains empty
The empty hand relaxes, opens before capture, closes after contact and releases
Thrust, uppercut and downstroke have distinct blade directions and forward weight transfer
Waterfowl has overhead horizontal preparation and different compact/extended burst silhouettes
Phase-two wings, hovering release and body-dive poses are differentiated
limitations: Video-guided manually authored adaptation, not imported original animation data
Anonymous reference streams are low resolution and sampled, not full 4K60 or exact joint reconstruction
Static authoring previews do not include server-owned entity travel or target tracking
Not every animation frame, branch, viewing angle, terrain or network condition is covered

scope: Sampled 360-degree, high/low-angle, crown and grip views; structural grip checks across all clips. Not exhaustive frame, camera or terrain coverage.
